title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated content to clone the identity of a real, named immigration attorney and deploy that likeness in social media advertisements. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI product from a known developer. It occurred in the deliberate misuse of generative tools to fabricate convincing video and profile content at scale, targeting people seeking immigration legal services.

The vulnerability that allowed the fraud to persist was the absence of any verification layer between social media advertising platforms and the professional credentials of the people those advertisements claimed to represent. A victim had no straightforward way to distinguish the real attorney's presence from the AI-fabricated one without conducting independent research outside the platform. The personal documents and money were transferred before any in-person or formally verified contact took place.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether law enforcement has identified or charged anyone, and whether the social media platforms were aware of the fake profiles before or after the fraud was reported.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx legal resident from the Dominican Republic lost $4,820 to scammers who created fake social media advertisements for immigration services. Victor Hernandez responded to what appeared to be an immigration attorney offering citizenship help without an exam, then sent increasing amounts of money via Zelle along with personal documents like his Social Security card and residency card. After his wife became suspicious, they discovered the scheme was fake and involved artificial intelligence-generated content based on real attorney Angel Leal from Miami.

The scammers used Leal's identity without permission to create multiple fake profiles and videos targeting vulnerable immigrants nationwide. Leal, who has practiced immigration law for 33 years, says he has identified and taken down close to 8,000 fake profile videos impersonating him. Hernandez filed reports with New York police and federal law enforcement and now faces financial hardship, including unpaid rent and utilities. Leal warns people to never hire attorneys through social media, conduct in-person meetings, and avoid attorneys requesting payment through cash-sending apps.
